question.problem:
Given that 
$|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ a & b-1\end{aligned}|=5$,
find 
$|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ a+2 & b\end{aligned}|.$
question.worked_solution:
We "factor out" the given determinant from the determinant we would like to find:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ a+2 & b\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ a+2 & (b-1)+1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the linearity property of determinants, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ a+2 & (b-1)+1\end{aligned}| & ={{|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ a & b-1\end{aligned}|}_{⏟}}_{5}+|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =5+(2-8) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
